events.text: A ferry has broken its rope in the flood and is spinning toward the rapids with a family on board. You could stop the river with your qi and drown the valley doing it. What it needs is one arrow with a line on it, from a bank a long way off.

choices.text: Shoot the line, the way you learned as a youth

ok.log: The arrow takes the line across the water and into the ferry's mast. They haul it in hand over hand. Of everything you can do now, this was the thing that was needed.

fail.log: Your hands remember the bow and your eyes do not. You go into the water after them instead, and get them out, and it costs you.

choices.text: Run across the water to them

ok.log: The old footwork, on water this time: one step on each wave. You bring the children back two at a time.

fail.log: The third wave is not where your feet expected it. You get them out, soaked and sorry.

effects.log: You call for boats and the boats come, too late for the ferry but not for the family.

events.text: In a hill village a child has a fever that no pill of yours can touch: your elixirs are for cultivators and would burn her out. The village healer is dead. What she needs is the plain medicine of a village physician, the kind you studied before you had a realm.

choices.text: Treat her with the old remedies

ok.log: Willow bark, cold cloths and three nights awake. On the fourth morning she asks for rice. The old art was the right one.

fail.log: You have forgotten more than you thought. She lives anyway, and you are not sure it was your doing.

choices.text: Send for a physician from the city

effects.log: The physician comes in four days, and is good at his work.

events.text: A boy of a small sect has walked a month to find you. He does not want a secret art. He wants to see the first form you ever learned, done the way you did it before you were anyone, because his master says that is where every great fighter really is.

choices.text: Show him the first sword form

ok.log: You do the first form, slowly, as a beginner does it. The boy weeps, and so, a little, do you. His master was right.

fail.log: Your hands do the form the way you do it now, and it is not what he came for. He thanks you politely and goes home.

ok.log: You draw it in the dirt: where the weight goes, why. He goes home with the first form and the reason for it.

fail.log: He listens politely to a lecture he does not understand.

choices.text: Send him back to his master

effects.log: "The one who sent you already knows," you tell him. He goes home unhappy, and later understands.

events.text: An old friend from before your realm has died, and the family asks you for a poem for the grave. They do not want a cultivator's words. They want the poems you wrote together as young fools, in the style you had then.

choices.text: Write it in your young hand

ok.log: It is clumsy, and young, and exactly right. The family carves it on the stone as you wrote it.

fail.log: You write a fine poem, a master's poem. It is not the one they asked for, and they are too kind to say so.

choices.text: Stand at the grave and say nothing

effects.log: You stand at the grave a long time and say nothing. It is also a kind of poem.
